name: Bubble Break ASMR Tabletop
request: Create a small, playable Bubble Break ASMR game for one player on desktop and touch. The player presses individual bubbles on a reusable bubble-wrap sheet. A press visibly depresses and pops that bubble with synchronized satisfying pop audio, then adds exactly one to the popped counter after the pop completes. Holding, spamming, or pressing a popped bubble must not count twice. Let the player finish a sheet of at least twelve bubbles, see completion feedback, and deliberately reset to a fresh sheet. Use a close, readable tabletop presentation and minimal counter/reset UI. Search Marketplace first for a complete reusable interaction, including any existing geometry, animation, sounds and behavior; inspect what it already provides and integrate only missing features. Search separately for missing media if needed. Audio must come from Marketplace and actually play. Record unavailable importer capabilities rather than pretending a suitable scripted component does not exist. Choose reasonable details yourself; no saving, multiplayer, purchases or large map. Success needs observed press/pop/recovery timing, per-bubble state, exact counting, sheet completion/reset and usable desktop/touch input. Do not claim success from code inspection alone.

assetNeeds.role: Complete reusable bubble-wrap interaction component supplying as much verified geometry, individual targeting, pop state behavior, animation, and Marketplace sound behavior as possible before missing integration is authored.
assetNeeds.constraints: Inspect complete interactive Models before static props. Candidate must support or be adaptable to at least twelve individually targetable bubbles in a compact tabletop footprint. Audit all scripts, dependencies, remotes, animation objects, sound references, input assumptions, and provenance. Preserve compatible existing behavior and media. Unsupported script, rig, package, or serialization import is a recorded capability gap requiring review, not permission to replace the component. No numeric require IDs or arbitrary HTTP code.

intent.experienceRole: This component is the tactile core of the ASMR loop, not merely decoration: it should provide reusable bubble geometry and preferably the press/pop behavior and media that make repeated interaction satisfying.
intent.interaction: The player clicks or taps one ready bubble; it depresses, audibly pops, settles as popped, and becomes unavailable. Completion/count integration occurs only after that sequence and may be supplied by retained behavior or narrowly scoped glue after inspection.
reusableFeatures: Individually addressable bubble geometry and hit regions
Ready, pressing, and permanently popped state behavior
Visible depression, collapse, and settle animation
Embedded Marketplace pop sound references and playback timing
Desktop click and touch interaction handling
Auditable scripts, remotes, dependencies, and cleanup behavior

assetNeeds.role: Separate Marketplace pop audio only if the inspected reusable interaction has no usable, attributable, and verified embedded sound.
assetNeeds.constraints: Search only after inspecting the complete interaction. Require a short satisfying dry bubble-wrap pop suitable for close ASMR playback, with valid Marketplace provenance and permission to load in the experience. It must pass loading, playback, synchronization, and listening checks. Do not use generated, built-in, procedural, placeholder, or invented audio IDs.

intent.experienceRole: The sound supplies the primary ASMR reward and confirms the exact visible moment each bubble collapses.
intent.interaction: A validated bubble press triggers one audible pop synchronized to visible collapse; held, rejected, or already-popped input produces no additional counted pop playback.
reusableFeatures: Marketplace provenance and usable sound reference
Appropriate duration for the press-to-settle sequence
No unwanted music, speech, or long ambience

spec.assetStrategy:
Begin with complete Marketplace Model discovery for an interactive bubble-wrap or bubble-pop system, not a static sheet. Inspect candidate hierarchy, source scripts, remotes, state model, animations, input handling, sounds, reset behavior, dependencies, and cleanup before assigning implementation ownership. Retain useful verified geometry, behavior, animation, and media, and adapt only the missing counter, validation, completion, reset, HUD, lifecycle, or device integration established by that inspection. Script paths for discovery-dependent glue intentionally remain unassigned until the selected component’s actual interfaces are known.

Embedded audio must retain Marketplace provenance and undergo loading, playback, synchronization, and listening checks. Only if inspection establishes that the complete component lacks usable audio should the separate Audio need be searched. Standalone animation retrieval is not assumed; animation should preferably come inside the complete Model. If a promising candidate contains scripts, rigs, packages, or serialization that the importer cannot preserve, record the exact capability gap and escalate it rather than treating the candidate as absent or silently rebuilding it. No asset IDs, compatibility claims, or successful media tests are assumed in this plan.
spec.title: Bubble Break ASMR Tabletop
spec.summary:
A compact one-player tabletop bubble-wrap experience for desktop and touch. The player spawns safely beside a small, warmly lit desk with the reusable bubble sheet filling the close gameplay view. Minimal guidance invites the player to click or tap any raised bubble. A valid press locks that bubble, visibly compresses it, plays a synchronized Marketplace pop, settles it into a popped state, and only then advances the counter by exactly one. The player continues until every bubble on the sheet is popped, receives clear completion feedback, and deliberately chooses Reset Sheet to restore a fresh layout and zero counter.

The planned sheet contains at least twelve individually addressable bubbles, preferably a readable 4-by-4 arrangement if the selected reusable Marketplace component supports it. The imported component’s geometry, scripts, animations, sounds, interfaces, and dependencies must be inspected before any replacement or glue implementation is assigned. The tabletop remains a small focused interaction area: safe spawn/stool position, central sheet, restrained desk dressing, close camera framing, and boundaries that prevent irrelevant travel. There is no saving, economy, purchase flow, progression system, combat, or large map.

Authoritative session state belongs to the server: sheet generation, each bubble’s ready/pressing/popped phase, rate checks, distance checks, exact counter increments, completion, and reset eligibility. The client is responsible for pointer/touch intent, close presentation, HUD, and local visual responsiveness only; it cannot award pops. Assumptions chosen as requested: a quiet warm desk setting, a preferred 16-bubble layout where compatible with the retained component, a short approximately 0.15–0.35 second press-to-settle sequence, and a persistent depressed appearance until reset. Final acceptance requires native gameplay observation and audible playback, not code inspection.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a close, tactile ASMR product-shot composition rather than a broad room. The central landmark is a translucent, slightly cool-tinted bubble sheet on a warm matte wood tabletop. A chair or safe standing position places the avatar within validated interaction distance, while the gameplay camera frames the whole sheet at a shallow overhead angle. Edge dressing may include a softly shaped desk mat, small lamp, and restrained background objects, but these remain noninteractive and must not compete with the bubbles.

Shape language should be soft and rounded: circular bubble domes, rounded sheet corners, beveled UI panels, and gentle pools of light. Ready bubbles must read as raised and glossy; a pressing bubble visibly compresses through a brief staged motion; a popped bubble remains flattened or inverted with reduced highlight so its state is unmistakable. Avoid excessive particles, screen shake, neon colors, or arcade clutter. The press animation and audio synchronization are the primary reward.

Use a warm neutral environment palette with the sheet as the cool focal accent. Maintain strong value contrast between tabletop, bubble edges, and pressed states. Lighting should make dome silhouettes and deformation readable without harsh reflections. Keep all interactive bubbles large enough for reliable touch selection and leave clear spacing between hit regions.

The HUD should be minimal: a compact high-contrast “Popped 0 / Total” counter and a clearly labeled Reset Sheet control. Reset remains deliberate and visually separated from bubble hit areas. At completion, show a restrained centered confirmation such as “Sheet Complete” with a gentle scale/fade treatment and make the reset action prominent. Desktop hover may provide a subtle highlight, while touch must not rely on hover. UI must respect safe areas and remain readable on common desktop and mobile aspect ratios.

requirements.acceptance: The server identifies bubbles from trusted sheet state, rejects invalid generation IDs, excessive request rates, dead or absent characters, out-of-range players, pressing/popped bubbles, and unauthorized resets. requirements.description: Maintain a clean one-player session across character respawns and remove stale connections or presentation state without adding persistence.
requirements.acceptance: Respawning rebinds camera/input/HUD dependencies without duplicate handlers or duplicate HUDs, preserves or cleanly resynchronizes the current authoritative sheet state, and leaving the session cleans associated connections and state. No DataStore or cross-session saving is introduced.

tasks.title: Search, import into the supplied namespace, audit, and natively inspect complete Marketplace bubble-wrap interaction candidates; preserve useful verified behavior and record unsupported importer capabilities instead of replacing them.
After component inspection, retain and verify embedded Marketplace pop media or search separately for a missing pop sound; document provenance, loading, playback, and listening results.
Assemble the compact safe tabletop interaction area around the retained component, including readable lighting, collidable spawn, close interaction placement, restrained dressing, and boundaries.

Inspect the retained component interfaces, then register only necessary server/client glue to provide authoritative per-bubble phases, validation, exact post-animation counting, anti-spam handling, completion, and reset without rebuilding retained behavior.

Integrate desktop/touch targeting, authoritative initial-state synchronization, minimal counter/reset UI, completion feedback, and close camera presentation using only glue proven missing after inspection.
Add the proven-missing respawn, cleanup, and resynchronization behavior without persistence or duplicate client controllers.

Run protected native desktop and touch verification of required instances, press/pop/settle timing, audible synchronization, held and spammed input, already-popped rejection, exact counting, final completion, deliberate reset, close presentation, and respawn behavior; report any blocked capability honestly.
